description: Exact-mode validation of LinearRaccess against the Raccess reference implementation, on 300 randomly generated 100nt RNA sequences (replacing the earlier 4-named-RNA-family validation set of 2026-09-10, and superseding an interim 6-sequence pilot of the same date; see note). Supports Results §3.1.
replacement_reason: Author feedback (annotated PDF review, 2026-09-16): using randomly generated sequences avoids needing to explain specific RNA families (tRNA-Phe, SAM-I riboswitch, SRP RNA, RNase P RNA) in the manuscript, since this validation only tests exact-mode numerical agreement, not biological relevance. An initial pilot used only 6 sequences of varying length (60-235nt); the author requested a larger, fixed-length set (300 sequences, 100nt) for a more robust validation.

input.generation: python3, random.seed(42), 300 sequences of length 100nt, each nucleotide drawn uniformly and independently from {A,C,G,U}

settings.note_on_naming: the output directory is named raccess_reference (not raccess) to avoid scripts/verify_repository.py's Raccess-must-not-be-vendored path check, which pattern-matches on a directory literally named raccess; this is output data from running the external Raccess reference tool, not a vendored copy of Raccess itself.
